passage: At the cyber cafe near the bus stand in a small town, Kashish had the scholarship form ready to send. Leela, who ran the cafe, saw the hesitation over the button. "Do your check first," Leela said, and slid a list from the desk drawer: name as on the ID, date of birth, marks, phone number, photo, right document attached, and what the notice had asked for. Kashish went down it with a finger. The phone number had one digit swapped. The marksheet attached was the front page only. She fixed both and pressed submit, and the receipt printed. "Two minutes," Leela said. "That saves you a trip and a rejection."

qa.q: What two errors did Kashish find on the list?
qa.a: A swapped digit in the phone number, and a marksheet with only the front page attached.

qa.q: What was Kashish feeling while hesitating over the button?
qa.a: Nervous and unsure, not certain that everything on the form was right.
It made Kashish check one item at a time, catching two errors before submitting.

qa.q: Why might Leela keep the checklist in the drawer?
qa.a: Leela has probably seen many errors from customers and wants to prevent repeat trips and rejections.

grounding: Shows a careful person using a short checklist to catch small errors before submitting a form.
